title: Arizona August 2026 ex parte renewal share
question: What percentage of Arizona Medicaid and CHIP beneficiaries due for renewal in August 2026 will have coverage renewed on an ex parte basis, using the original (O) submission when CMS first publishes it, computed to one decimal?
resolutionSource: CMS, State Medicaid and CHIP Eligibility Processing Data (data.medicaid.gov)
resolutionRule: Resolves to Arizona's ex parte renewal share for the August 2026 reporting period, computed from the original (O) submission row in CMS dataset 5abea2e0-3f8e-4b49-a50d-d63d5fd9103c when CMS first publishes it. Compute 100 times Beneficiaries Whose Coverage Was Renewed on an Ex Parte Basis divided by Beneficiaries with a Renewal Due, using the numerator and denominator as first published, rounded to one decimal. Subsequent corrections and updated (U) submissions do not change resolution.

reasoning.text: Arizona August 2026 ex parte renewal forecast

The target is Arizona's state row, not a national total or weighted average. CMS dataset 5abea2e0-3f8e-4b49-a50d-d63d5fd9103c identifies O as original and U as updated. CMS's state tables define ex parte rates using beneficiaries due for renewal as the denominator: Metric 5a(1) divided by Metric 5. All historical anchors below use initial reporting-period tables, excluding quarterly updated-renewal tables.

Evidence limitation: the dataset metadata was fetched, but raw CSV and API requests were inaccessible through the web tool. Raw Arizona ex parte numerator counts were not fetched. HistoricalContext therefore records CMS's published whole-percent snapshot values, not reconstructed one-decimal raw-row shares. The forecast still resolves using the first-published original-row counts.

reasoning.call: Fetch the Arizona rows in the official January and February 2026 CMS snapshots, Coverage Retention and Disenrollment Rates by State, from the corresponding jan2026.pdf and feb2026.pdf URLs in sourceContext.
reasoning.result: January 2026: 183,464 beneficiaries due for renewal; ex parte share 68%. February 2026: 113,696 due; ex parte share 63%. These are the snapshots' whole-percent initial-period values.

reasoning.call: Fetch the Arizona rows in the official March and April 2026 CMS snapshots from the corresponding mar2026.pdf and apr2026.pdf URLs in sourceContext.
reasoning.result: March 2026: 180,456 beneficiaries due for renewal; ex parte share 70%. April 2026: 151,629 due; ex parte share 69%.

reasoning.call: Fetch the Arizona rows in the official May and June 2026 CMS snapshots from the corresponding may2026.pdf and jun2026.pdf URLs in sourceContext.
reasoning.result: May 2026: 181,665 beneficiaries due for renewal; ex parte share 73%. June 2026: 98,446 due; ex parte share 60%, total renewed 73%, disenrolled 23%, and pending 4%.

reasoning.call: Fetch Arizona's initial-period state tables in the six official July through December 2025 CMS snapshots listed in sourceContext.
reasoning.result: July 2025: 226,932 due, ex parte 65%; August: 189,866 due, 68%; September: 111,492 due, 61%; October: 178,468 due, 67%; November: 176,740 due, 70%; December: 97,996 due, 59%.

reasoning.text: The reference class is 12 consecutive Arizona initial-period monthly prints, July 2025 through June 2026. Their arithmetic mean gives a base rate of 66.0833%; the January-June 2026 mean is 67.1667%. June's small cohort and 60% share resemble December's similarly small cohort and 59% share. This supports partial mean reversion, although cohort composition is an inference rather than a verified cause.

Separate adjustments: the recent level supports a modest increase over the annual base rate; momentum receives no sustained linear extrapolation because monthly changes reverse repeatedly. June's decline receives partial persistence weight. Last August supplies a modest seasonal anchor. CMS's renewal-compliance page names December 31, 2026 as the compliance deadline, but this run verified no Arizona implementation change specifically affecting August, so the policy adjustment is zero.

Prior/update/interval: Use a mean-reverting seasonal persistence model with the 12 fetched monthly prints. Point = 0.50*(January-June mean 67.1667) + 0.25*(June 60) + 0.25*(August 2025 68) = 65.5833%, rounded to 65.6%. Relative to the 66.0833% base rate, components are recent level +1.0833 percentage points, momentum 0, partial June deviation -1.7917, seasonal comparator +0.2083, and policy 0. Successive changes are [3,-7,6,3,-11,9,-5,7,-1,4,-13]; their sum is -5 and sum of squares is 565. Sample sigma = 7.501515 percentage points, computed as sqrt((565-25/11)/10). The normal 80% one-month half-width is 1.28*sigma = 9.601939. For the two-month June-to-August horizon, multiply by sqrt(2), giving 13.579193. Unrounded bounds are 65.583333 +/- 13.579193 = [52.004140,79.162526], rounded to [52.0,79.2]. Historical rounding precision is a limitation of this dispersion estimate.

Publication-date audit: the official CMS snapshot index verifies that June 2026 was released September 25, 2026, but exposes no announcement verifying December 15, 2026 for the August original print. The specifications distinguish state submission deadlines from public publication dates. The contractual resolutionDate remains 2026-12-15; its exact public-release timing could not be verified in this run and was not inferred from cadence.

Upside risk: a cohort with more beneficiaries eligible for automated renewal could restore the higher recent shares. Downside risk: weaker data matching or a harder-to-renew cohort could prolong June's decline. A broad automation improvement taking the share above 79.2%, or a matching disruption or reporting-method change taking it below 52.0%, would land outside the interval.
